name: Myeongdong Kyoja
notes: Knife-cut noodles (kalguksu) since 1966. Order kalguksu + mandu. Cash preferred, closed Sundays.

name: Woo Lae Oak
notes: Since 1946. Order the naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) — this is the move, not the BBQ. Reservations recommended.

name: Hanchu
notes: Famous fried chicken on Garosu-gil. Bone-in + whole green peppers — grassy heat cuts the oil. Opens 5pm.

name: Chicken Rock
notes: Neighbourhood gem with a warm owner. Fried chicken + tteokbokki. Still by Hand clothes shop downstairs.

name: Mangwon Market
notes: Local traditional market — non-touristy alternative to Gwangjang. Banchan, tteokbokki, produce. Cash preferred.

name: Nari's House
notes: Est. 1985. Naengsam (frozen samgyeopsal) — ultra-thin frozen pork belly, a 40-year institution. Expect a queue. Open 2pm–midnight, every other Sun closed.

name: Che Budong Sujebi
notes: Listed locally as 체부동잔치집 (Chebudong Janchijip) — famous for deulkkae sujebi (perilla-seed sujebi). Hand-torn noodle soup in rich anchovy broth.

name: Sigol Yachae Doenjjang
notes: NW's friend has loved this for doenjang jjigae. Humble local spot, the kind tourists never find.

name: Woojinga
notes: NW went here personally — premium 1++ hanwoo beef. Marbled like A5 wagyu but meatier. Comparable to NYC's Cote at lower price. Book via CatchTable.

name: Howang
notes: Same tier as Woojinga per NW's Gangnam-local friend. All-hanwoo, high quality. Reservations needed. Actually in Bangbae (Seocho-gu), not Cheongdam — confirm via Siksin before booking.

name: Hanwadam Black
notes: Premium aged-hanwoo sub-brand of Hanwadam. Both branches within 50m. Typically packed — reserve.

name: Gaggangsullae
notes: NW went for galbi — grandmothers eating during the day is the quality signal. Less premium than Woojinga but phenomenal. Galbi is the order.

name: Obaltan
notes: Gopchang, makchang, daechang — offal KBBQ. Charred, funky, chewy. Completely different from beef/pork belly. Yeoksam flagship.

name: Balwoo Gongyang
notes: The only temple food restaurant in Korea run by the Jogye Order. Plant-based (no garlic/onion/leek). Private rooms, intentional silence. Courses ₩30k–₩90k. Closed Sundays. Book a month ahead.

name: Anthracite Coffee
notes: Seoul's most architecturally ambitious coffee brand. Former industrial spaces converted with serious design intent. Hongdae branch overlooks a sculptural garden.

name: Archivist Café
notes: Known for Einspänner (Vienna-style coffee with thick whipped cream). Dark green walls, small space — go early.

name: Cheongsudang
notes: One of Seoul's most photogenic cafés — hanok conversion with bamboo entrance, stone path over a stream, soufflé cakes.

name: Nudake
notes: Conceptual café directly below the Gentle Monster flagship. Sculptural pastries (the 'Peak' croissant is the photo). Shares Haus Dosan building with Tamburins.

name: Cafe Onion
notes: Bakery-café in a restored hanok near Bukchon. The pandoro covered in powdered sugar is the order. Original branch is in Seongsu in a former metal factory.

name: Mr. Ahn's Makgeolli
notes: Craft makgeolli bar + dinner spot. Part of the broader makgeolli revival. Listed in the Michelin Guide. Near Noksapyeong Station Exit 2.

name: Ace Four Club
notes: Serious craft cocktail bar with window seats overlooking Eulji-ro. Part of the Euljiro creative revival.

name: Gong Gan
notes: Cocktail bar in a hanok with a glass inner courtyard. The room is the point as much as the drinks.

name: Kompakt Record Bar
notes: Vinyl-focused bar run by Jinmoo of 360 Sounds DJ crew. NO connection to the Cologne label. This is Ver.1 (the original, 2018) on the Apgujeong/Sinsa border. Ver.2 is also Sinsa-dong; Ver.3 opened in Seongsu (81 Yeonmujang-gil).

name: Stoked & Stoned
notes: Surf/skate-aesthetic cocktail bar. Casual, late, music-forward. 2nd floor — accessed via elevator in an indoor mall hallway.

name: Wild Duck Canteen
notes: HBC institution — diner-style late-night spot. Burgers, drinks, decent crowd.

name: Komfy
notes: Sofas, low-key music, no pressure to move on. Vinyl/hi-fi bar in the Hongdae/Hapjeong area — actually NOT in Seongsu as previously listed.

name: Vita
notes: Natural wine bar from LP's recs. Could not be independently verified by name alone — possibly Instagram-only or recently opened. Ask LP for the Instagram handle / Naver listing before going.
addr: Unverified — pin placed approximately in Itaewon

name: Times
notes: Cocktail-forward late bar in the Apgujeong/Sinsa speakeasy district.

name: Orgasm Valley
notes: Full name 'Gyegog - Orgasm Valley' (계곡 = 'valley' in Korean). Hip-hop lounge — late, loud, dancing. Opens 4pm weekdays, til 5am Fri/Sat.

name: Zest
notes: The single most-recommended place in this guide — four independent sources. Zero-waste philosophy: house-distilled gin from Korean botanicals, own-made sodas, city honey from Seoul beehives.
insider: Ask for Noah (co-owner). Mention Alexander Kim — he's Bobby Min's cousin. Reservations essential.

name: VIBD BLVD
notes: Vinyl sanctuary — walls of LPs, DJ booth at the bar. 4-person table limit. Write song requests on paper. VIBD Signature (cranberry) is the house cocktail. Doors 8:30pm.

name: Pine & Co
notes: Hidden Apgujeong alley — find the entrance, press a button, descend. Service bar like a sci-fi R&D lab; room is warm leather and candles. House-distilled gin. Closed Mondays.
insider: AK: 'One of my two favorite bars in the world.'

name: Le Chamber
notes: Speakeasy behind a bookshelf — pull the correct book. 50-seat room: high ceilings, chandeliers, live piano. 200+ whiskies. Founded by world-champ bartenders. Cover charge.
insider: AK: 'Finding it is a lot of fun.'

name: Bar Cham
notes: Set in a traditional hanok. Korean spirits-first: soju, makgeolli, provincial spirits used in inventive cocktails. Menu changes seasonally. Owner BJ Lim. Small — book ahead or wait at sister bar Pomme nearby.

name: Courte
notes: Operates as café (Courte Cafe) + bar (Courte Sidebar). Thu–Sat only, noon to late. RSVP by DM. Part of the Apgujeong crawl cluster.

name: Cakeshop
notes: Seoul's most internationally known club. Underground, no-frills room; serious DJ bookings (techno, house, experimental). Arrive after 1am. Passport required. Basement next to Tussa skateshop near Noksapyeong Station.

name: Hills & Europa
notes: Two interconnected rooms — Hills (house/techno) + Europa (experimental). Bigger and slightly less scene-at-the-door than Cakeshop.

name: Kockiri
notes: Active again per their Instagram. Hip-hop and R&B-leaning. Verify hours before going.

name: Henz Club
notes: One of Seoul's most established clubs. Hip-hop/trap nights alongside electronic.

name: Mingles
notes: Chef Mingoo Kang's restaurant — modern Korean fine dining built on jang (fermented pastes). One of Asia's most consistently celebrated kitchens.

name: Mosu
notes: Chef Sung Anh's flagship — reopened March 2025 in Yongsan/Itaewon after closing the Hannam location in 2024. Korean sensibility filtered through Western fine-dining, then stripped back. Currently 2 stars (was 3 in 2023–24). Counter seating is the best seat.

name: Onjium
notes: Rooted in royal court cuisine (궁중요리), connected to Arumjigi's cultural research. The most culturally grounded tasting menu in Seoul.

name: Nothing Written
notes: Women's clothing store designed to feel like shopping a friend's wardrobe. Flagship is 'House & Garden Hannam.'

name: Boon the Shop
notes: Korean luxury multi-brand with an editorial eye. One of Seoul's most respected high-end concept stores.

name: Beaker
notes: Samsung C&T's multi-brand concept store. Well-edited international mix. Multiple locations.

name: 10 Corso Como
notes: The Milan concept store's Seoul outpost. Fashion, design objects, books, café — the full 10CC experience.

name: DDP Market Stalls
notes: Korean designer kiosks inside Zaha Hadid's DDP complex. Middle-market, some haggling. Grounds open 24hr on weekends.

name: Migliore
notes: Multiple floors of affordable fashion where haggling is expected. Style-to-price ratio is unmatched. Bring cash.

name: Atelier Edition
notes: Curated concept store in Dosan Park area. Part of the high-design retail cluster with Gentle Monster + Tamburins. Confirm hours via @atelieredition.dosan.

name: Monoha Hannam
notes: Named after the Mono-ha art movement. Concept store + gallery + café. Curates ceramics, clothes, home goods, books, art.

name: Monoha Seongsu
notes: The Seongsu branch of Monoha. Larger space, more frequent exhibitions.

name: Shop Amomento
notes: Multi-brand sister store to the Amomento label — stocks Amomento + curated like-minded labels.

name: Gentle Monster
notes: Eyewear flagship that's also a rotating sculptural art installation. Worth visiting even if not buying. Shares Haus Dosan building with Tamburins and Nudake.

name: Tamburins
notes: Gentle Monster's beauty arm. Perfumes, hand creams, cosmetics in gallery-store format. Café inside. Price advantage over abroad is real. Also has a Cheongdam flagship. Triple-sourced consensus pick.

name: Youssoful
notes: Indie Korean fragrance brand ('You're so beautiful') — more boutique and less label-forward than Tamburins. Signature scent: Saint Moritz. Affordable.

name: Post Archive Faction
notes: Korea's most technically ambitious brand. Flagship built in the original sewing factory where PAF garments were made. Full range, genuinely cheaper than abroad.

name: Andersson Bell
notes: Contemporary Seoul fashion — tailoring meets streetwear. Flagship relocated to a converted building near Gyeongbokgung.

name: Amomento
notes: Minimalist Korean womenswear. Emphasis on drape and proportion. Seochon flagship sits in a hanok — traditional architecture visible from the fitting room.

name: Hyein Seo
notes: Avant-garde, youth-culture inflected. Antwerp Royal Academy training. Worn by Rihanna, Kendrick, NewJeans. Flagship + atelier in one building.

name: thisisneverthat
notes: The Korean streetwear reference point. Graphic-heavy, logo-forward, accessible price point.

name: Leeum Museum
notes: Three buildings by Mario Botta, Jean Nouvel, and Rem Koolhaas. National treasures alongside Warhol, Rothko, Hirst. One of Asia's serious art institutions.

name: MMCA Seoul
notes: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art. Strong rotating shows on Korean and international contemporary art.

name: Gallery Hyundai
notes: Seoul's most established commercial gallery. Heavyweight Korean modern and contemporary names.

name: Arumjigi
notes: Cultural foundation dedicated to preserving Korean aesthetics. Beautiful building, rotating exhibitions on traditional craft and design. Connected to Onjium.

name: APMA (Amorepacific)
notes: Amorepacific Museum of Art in David Chipperfield's HQ building. Strong shows, beautiful concrete-and-light architecture.

name: Daelim Museum
notes: Photography-focused museum in a converted hanok-adjacent space. Younger curatorial voice than the major institutions.

name: Piknic
notes: Multi-floor cultural space — exhibitions, café, rooftop. Strong design and music-adjacent programming.

name: DDP
notes: Zaha Hadid's swooping aluminum landmark. Worth a walk-through even without an exhibition. Grounds open 24hr on weekends.

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
notes: The main Joseon dynasty palace. Free hanbok rental nearby gets you free palace entry. Changing of the guard at 10am and 2pm. Closed Tuesdays.

name: Gwangjang Market
notes: Iconic food market — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, raw beef tartare. Go hungry, eat standing.

name: Namdaemun Market
notes: 600-year-old market. Galchi (hairtail) alley is the food highlight. Mostly daytime, but parts run late.

name: COEX / Starfield Library
notes: Massive underground mall + the photogenic Starfield Library (free). NW's pick for a rainy day in Gangnam.

name: Seoul Forest Park
notes: Large urban park between Seongsu and the Han River. Good break in a Seongsu/Hannamdong day. Deer enclosure if you want it.

name: National Museum of Korea
notes: The country's largest museum. Free permanent collection — Korean history from prehistory to modern. NW's pick for a rainy day.

name: N Seoul Tower
notes: Iconic at sunset. Cable car or hike up Namsan. Pairs naturally with the Myeongdong/Namdaemun cluster.

name: Bukchon Hanok Village
notes: Living neighborhood of preserved hanok between two palaces. Walk early morning before the tour groups arrive.

name: DMZ
notes: Day tour to the demilitarized zone — Imjingak, Third Tunnel, Dora Observatory. Most tours from Seoul are 6–8 hours. Book in advance, bring passport.

name: Lotte World
notes: Indoor amusement park (open year-round) + outdoor Magic Island. K-drama filming location for decades. Adjacent Lotte World Tower has a glass-floor observatory.

name: Cafe Onion Seongsu
notes: The original Cafe Onion — a converted 1970s metal workshop with raw concrete and industrial bones. Pandoro dusted in powdered sugar is the signature order. Rougher and more storied than the Anguk branch.

name: Kompakt Record Bar Ver.3
notes: Third outpost of Jinmoo's vinyl bar empire — same ethos as Ver.1 (Apgujeong/Sinsa) in a larger Seongsu industrial space. For Ver.1 see Apgujeong entry.

name: Anthracite Coffee Seochon
notes: Second Seoul branch of Anthracite — same serious design intent as the Hapjeong flagship, set in the heritage neighbourhood near Gyeongbokgung. Good anchor for a Seochon/Anguk day.
